context: Business analytics dashboard combining inline sparklines embedded in narrative prose paragraphs with a sortable summary table below — a data visualization designed in an editorial style.
first_impression: Clean, publication-adjacent layout where sparklines flow naturally within sentences, demonstrating genuine design intent rather than a default chart dump.
what_works: The inline-sparkline-in-text technique is sophisticated and well-executed — sparklines sit at the correct baseline, use a deliberate TOL color palette (blue for positive, red for negative trends), and semantically encode directionality rather than defaulting to schemeCategory10. Typographic hierarchy is present: the bold title, muted subtitle with midpoint separator, and quieter narrative body all have distinct voices.
what_doesnt: The inline sparklines are 60×12px — barely readable at rendered size, with trend shapes visible but fine details like the churn spike nearly indistinguishable; the table sparklines at 80×16px are only marginally better. The table section is the design weak point: standard alternating-row gray, a plain #f0f0f0 header, and system-ui with no weight differentiation between the 'Metric Summary' label and surrounding content — competent but noticeably less considered than the narrative section above it.
